title: LETTER 10: Letter to Editor — Importance of Jan Dhan Accounts

blocks.content: Topic: Write a letter to the editor of a national newspaper highlighting how Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) has transformed financial inclusion in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a national mission aiming to provide universal access to banking services.
Jan Dhan accounts offer zero-balance account opening, direct benefit transfers (DBT), and built-in accident insurance cover through RuPay cards.
A Letter to the Editor regarding Jan Dhan accounts highlights the socio-economic empowerment of marginalized communities through financial inclusion.
Key elements of a formal Letter to the Editor include Sender's Address, Date, Receiver's Address, Subject Line, Formal Salutation, Structured Body, and Sign-off.

blocks.content: Jan Dhan accounts serve as a vital gateway for financial inclusion, bridging the gap between unbanked citizens and formal banking services.
Subject: PMJDY — A Decade of Financial Empowerment for India's Unbanked

rows: Inbuilt RuPay debit card accidental cover
Optional or dependent on card tier
Available up to ₹10,000 for eligible holders

blocks.content: As India prepares to mark the tenth anniversary of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched on 28 August 2014, it is fitting to reflect on the transformative journey of this ambitious financial inclusion programme — one that has reshaped the relationship between the Indian state, its banking system, and its most marginalised citizens.

In its first decade, PMJDY has opened over 54 crore accounts, mobilised deposits exceeding Rs. 2.30 lakh crore, and issued over 37 crore RuPay debit cards to account holders who were previously entirely outside the formal financial system. Crucially, nearly 56% of these account holders are women, and over 67% belong to rural and semi-urban areas — groups that have historically been the most financially excluded. The Jan Dhan account has also become the conduit for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of government subsidies worth over Rs. 34 lakh crore — eliminating middlemen, reducing leakage, and ensuring that benefits reach genuine beneficiaries with speed and transparency.

The programme's integration with PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (accident insurance at Rs. 20/year) and PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (life insurance at Rs. 436/year) has extended social security to previously uninsured households. The overdraft facility of Rs. 10,000 available to compliant account holders provides a micro safety net for emergency consumption needs.

Yet challenges persist. A significant proportion of Jan Dhan accounts remain dormant or are used only once or twice a year — indicating that account opening is necessary but insufficient. Financial literacy, last-mile connectivity through Business Correspondents, and the expansion of credit products tailored to Jan Dhan customers must be the focus of the next decade of financial inclusion.
Your esteemed publication's continued coverage can inspire further progress in this vital mission.

items: Ensure proper formal letter format: Keep the subject line concise and relevant to the importance of Jan Dhan accounts.
Highlight specific benefits in the body paragraphs, such as Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), overdraft facilities, and financial security for low-income households.
End the letter with a strong call to action urging authorities and citizens to expand financial literacy alongside account opening.

blocks.content: Examiner's Tip: PMJDY-related questions are very common in bank exams. Always include specific statistics (54 crore accounts, Rs.2.30 lakh crore deposits, 56% women). A good answer shows both achievements and remaining challenges.
